title: A chart with negative numbers draws its bars below the line
goal: An animated chart given a negative number, such as a quarter that lost money, draws that bar as a flat line on the baseline, so the chart says the value was nothing. Negative values should draw below the baseline the way any chart app draws them, and a row that wears the theme colour should show that colour in its swatch rather than a struck-through box that reads as no colour.
notes: From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-10-17-animated-charts.json: "Negative values draw as a flat bar on the baseline" and "A row wearing the theme colour shows a struck-through swatch in its colour well, which can read as no colour at all." Left in the charts task log as rough on 2026-10-18; filed by the digest because a chart that draws a wrong value is broken, not a nit. Charts shipped in commit 29761749 as a title kind with a Chart section. The open card animated-charts-you-can-drop-into-a-video-do-the-six-charts-build-in-and-l is about the look, not this.
acceptance: Reproduced first: a Bar chart with rows 40, -25, 60 photographed at the hold, and what the -25 bar does pasted into this task log

Bar and Horizontal Bars charts draw a negative value as a bar running the other way from a visible baseline, its length to scale with the positive bars (measured within 2 px at 1080p), in the canvas, playback and an MP4 export
The Line chart takes a negative point below its baseline, and the Big Number counts up to a negative number with its minus sign
A row whose colour comes from the theme shows the theme colour in its swatch, not a struck-through box
A walk at Next defaults builds the 40, -25, 60 chart, photographs it at the hold and measures the -25 bar below the baseline

log.note: digest 2026-10-20: folded into a-chart-is-your-data-given-to-it-the-obvious-way (p1, the user's ask), which rebuilds how a chart takes and shows its numbers; drawing a negative value honestly and the theme swatch are an acceptance item there
